props.name: onBlur

Callback that is called when the text input is blurred

Note: If you are trying to find the last value of TextInput, you can use the `onEndEditing`
event, which is fired upon completion of editing.

props.description:
Callback that is called when the text input's text changes.
Changed text is passed as an argument to the callback handler.

props.name: onContentSizeChange
props.description:
Callback that is called when the text input's content size changes.
This will be called with
`{ nativeEvent: { contentSize: { width, height } } }`.

Only called for multiline text inputs.

props.name: onEndEditing
props.description: Callback that is called when text input ends.

props.name: onPress
props.description: Called when a single tap gesture is detected.

props.name: onSelectionChange
props.description: Callback that is called when the text input selection is changed.

props.name: onSubmitEditing
props.description: Callback that is called when the text input's submit button is pressed.

props.name: onScroll
props.description:
Invoked on content scroll with
 `{ nativeEvent: { contentOffset: { x, y } } }`.

May also contain other properties from ScrollEvent but on Android contentSize is not provided for performance reasons.

props.name: onKeyPress
props.description:
Callback that is called when a key is pressed.
This will be called with
 `{ nativeEvent: { key: keyValue } }`
where keyValue is 'Enter' or 'Backspace' for respective keys and the typed-in character otherwise including ' ' for space.

Fires before onChange callbacks.
Note: on Android only the inputs from soft keyboard are handled, not the hardware keyboard inputs.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: The string that will be rendered before text input has been entered

props.name: returnKeyType
props.description:
enum('default', 'go', 'google', 'join', 'next', 'route', 'search', 'send', 'yahoo', 'done', 'emergency-call')
Determines how the return key should look.

props.name: textAlign
props.description: Align the input text to the left, center, or right sides of the input field.

props.name: value
props.description:
The value to show for the text input. TextInput is a controlled component,
which means the native value will be forced to match this value prop if provided.
For most uses this works great, but in some cases this may cause flickering - one common cause is preventing edits by keeping value the same.
In addition to simply setting the same value, either set editable={false},
or set/update maxLength to prevent unwanted edits without flicker.

props.name: hitSlop
props.description:
This defines how far a touch event can start away from the view.
Typical interface guidelines recommend touch targets that are at least
30 - 40 points/density-independent pixels. If a Touchable view has
a height of 20 the touchable height can be extended to 40 with
hitSlop={{top: 10, bottom: 10, left: 0, right: 0}}
NOTE The touch area never extends past the parent view bounds and
the Z-index of sibling views always takes precedence if a touch
hits two overlapping views.

props.name: onStartShouldSetResponder
props.description: Does this view want to become responder on the start of a touch?

props.name: onMoveShouldSetResponder
props.description: Called for every touch move on the View when it is not the responder: does this view want to "claim" touch responsiveness?

props.name: onResponderEnd
props.description: If the View returns true and attempts to become the responder, one of the following will happen:

props.name: onResponderGrant
props.description:
The View is now responding for touch events.
This is the time to highlight and show the user what is happening

props.name: onResponderReject
props.description: Something else is the responder right now and will not release it

props.name: onResponderMove
props.description: The user is moving their finger

props.name: onResponderRelease
props.description: Fired at the end of the touch, ie "touchUp"

props.name: onResponderTerminationRequest
props.description:
Something else wants to become responder.
Should this view release the responder? Returning true allows release

props.name: onResponderTerminate
props.description:
The responder has been taken from the View.
Might be taken by other views after a call to onResponderTerminationRequest,
or might be taken by the OS without asking (happens with control center/ notification center on iOS)

props.name: onStartShouldSetResponderCapture
props.description:
onStartShouldSetResponder and onMoveShouldSetResponder are called with a bubbling pattern,
where the deepest node is called first.
That means that the deepest component will become responder when multiple Views return true for *ShouldSetResponder handlers.
This is desirable in most cases, because it makes sure all controls and buttons are usable.

However, sometimes a parent will want to make sure that it becomes responder.
This can be handled by using the capture phase.
Before the responder system bubbles up from the deepest component,
it will do a capture phase, firing on*ShouldSetResponderCapture.
So if a parent View wants to prevent the child from becoming responder on a touch start,
it should have a onStartShouldSetResponderCapture handler which returns true.

props.name: onMoveShouldSetResponderCapture
props.description:
onStartShouldSetResponder and onMoveShouldSetResponder are called with a bubbling pattern,
where the deepest node is called first.
That means that the deepest component will become responder when multiple Views return true for *ShouldSetResponder handlers.

props.description:
This defines how far a touch event can start away from the view.

the Z-index of sibling views always takes precedence if a touch
hits two overlapping views.

props.name: onStartShouldSetResponderCapture
props.description:
onStartShouldSetResponder and onMoveShouldSetResponder are called with a bubbling pattern,
where the deepest node is called first.
That means that the deepest component will become responder when multiple Views return true for *ShouldSetResponder handlers.
This is desirable in most cases, because it makes sure all controls and buttons are usable.

However, sometimes a parent will want to make sure that it becomes responder.
This can be handled by using the capture phase.
Before the responder system bubbles up from the deepest component,
it will do a capture phase, firing on*ShouldSetResponderCapture.
So if a parent View wants to prevent the child from becoming responder on a touch start,
it should have a onStartShouldSetResponderCapture handler which returns true.

props.name: onResponderTerminate
props.description:
The responder has been taken from the View.
Might be taken by other views after a call to onResponderTerminationRequest,
or might be taken by the OS without asking (happens with control center/ notification center on iOS)

props.name: onStartShouldSetResponderCapture
props.description:
onStartShouldSetResponder and onMoveShouldSetResponder are called with a bubbling pattern,
where the deepest node is called first.
That means that the deepest component will become responder when multiple Views return true for *ShouldSetResponder handlers.
This is desirable in most cases, because it makes sure all controls and buttons are usable.

However, sometimes a parent will want to make sure that it becomes responder.
This can be handled by using the capture phase.
Before the responder system bubbles up from the deepest component,
it will do a capture phase, firing on*ShouldSetResponderCapture.
So if a parent View wants to prevent the child from becoming responder on a touch start,
it should have a onStartShouldSetResponderCapture handler which returns true.

props.name: onScroll
props.description:
Invoked on content scroll with
 `{ nativeEvent: { contentOffset: { x, y } } }`.

May also contain other properties from ScrollEvent but on Android contentSize is not provided for performance reasons.

props.name: onKeyPress
props.description:
Callback that is called when a key is pressed.
This will be called with
 `{ nativeEvent: { key: keyValue } }`
where keyValue is 'Enter' or 'Backspace' for respective keys and the typed-in character otherwise including ' ' for space.

Fires before onChange callbacks.
Note: on Android only the inputs from soft keyboard are handled, not the hardware keyboard inputs.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: The string that will be rendered before text input has been entered

props.name: returnKeyType
props.description:
enum('default', 'go', 'google', 'join', 'next', 'route', 'search', 'send', 'yahoo', 'done', 'emergency-call')
Determines how the return key should look.

props.name: textAlign
props.description: Align the input text to the left, center, or right sides of the input field.

props.name: value
props.description:
The value to show for the text input. TextInput is a controlled component,
which means the native value will be forced to match this value prop if provided.
For most uses this works great, but in some cases this may cause flickering - one common cause is preventing edits by keeping value the same.
In addition to simply setting the same value, either set editable={false},
or set/update maxLength to prevent unwanted edits without flicker.

props.name: hitSlop
props.description:
This defines how far a touch event can start away from the view.
Typical interface guidelines recommend touch targets that are at least
30 - 40 points/density-independent pixels. If a Touchable view has
a height of 20 the touchable height can be extended to 40 with
hitSlop={{top: 10, bottom: 10, left: 0, right: 0}}
NOTE The touch area never extends past the parent view bounds and
the Z-index of sibling views always takes precedence if a touch
hits two overlapping views.
